## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
This maintenance visit recorded a critical deficiency in pump operation. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This is a confirmed failure mode requiring immediate professional attention. All other system components measured within normal parameters.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |
| Liquid Level Position | At Outlet |

The effluent filter was cleaned and reseated during this maintenance visit. Filter condition was good with light soiling.

## PUMP OPERATION -- CRITICAL FINDING
| Parameter | Measured | Nameplate | Load % | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 1.6 A | 7.2 A | 22.2% | CRITICAL |

**The pump is running but producing no hydraulic load.** The motor is drawing current but not moving fluid. This condition indicates one or more of the following:

- Impeller is broken or missing
- Discharge line is severed or disconnected
- Pump inlet is dry (no fluid available to the pump)

A pump running without fluid load will overheat rapidly and sustain motor damage. **Immediate professional attention is required.** A qualified technician must examine the pump discharge line for continuity and blockage, and must examine the pump impeller for damage or displacement.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface was dry with no evidence of ponding or breakout during this maintenance visit.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm (functional)
- Verified electrical connections (sound)
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (Do not delay):**
- A qualified technician must examine the pump discharge line for disconnection, blockage, or damage.
- A qualified technician must examine the pump impeller for breakage or displacement.
- Do not operate the system until the pump load deficiency is resolved. Continued operation risks motor failure and system shutdown.

**Routine:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once pump operation is restored and verified.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### About the Pump Problem
Your pump is running but not moving water. This happens when the impeller (the spinning part inside the pump) breaks, or when the discharge line (the pipe carrying water out of the pump) gets disconnected or blocked. Running a pump without water flowing through it is like running a car engine without oil -- the motor overheats and fails quickly.

Do not ignore this. Call a qualified technician today. They will open the pump, check the impeller, and trace the discharge line to find where the blockage or break is.

### Tank Solids
This maintenance visit recorded solids at about 23 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Your tank is healthy in this respect. Keep non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease -- and solids will accumulate slowly and predictably.
